TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate.issue: PHASE LOSS. This is a phase-suffixed C# hook and the sim has a single unphased dispatch, which is hook_dispatch gap G3 (24 dispatchers lose their phase structure; 27 phase-suffixed hooks declared on AbstractModel). Per binding rule 3 the mechanism keeps G3's `gap` verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Corruption is a LATE-phase cost modifier: C# runs it in Hook.ModifyEnergyCostInCombat's second pass (TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate, CorruptionPower.cs:16-25), strictly after every early-phase modifier. The sim's single modify_card_energy_cost pass orders it by registration instead, so Corruption contends with the ported early-phase modifiers -- Curious (powers.py:2883) and Spiked Gauntlets -- by accident of application order. Corruption returning a hard 0 makes it order-sensitive in the worst way: it must WIN over Spiked Gauntlets' +1, and it does so only if it happens to be registered later. Same shape as hook_dispatch G3's own executed Tangled/Free-Attack witness.

ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition.issue: The destination-pile DECISION is replaced by an after-the-fact move, and the sim has the right hook available and does not use it. C# (CorruptionPower.cs:27-38) returns (PileType.Exhaust, position) from the pile-resolution chain, so a played Skill never enters the discard pile at all. The sim lets combat._resolve_card_play put the card in the discard pile (combat.py:453), runs the exhaust-keyword check and then the modify_card_play_result_pile chain (combat.py:500-511), and only afterwards -- inside on_card_played (combat.py:514) -- does Corruption pull the card out of the discard pile and append it to the exhaust pile, firing on_card_exhausted itself (powers.py:610-613). Two consequences. (i) CONTENTION ORDER: the sim's modify_card_play_result_pile hook exists (hooks.py:236-246) but accepts only 'discard'/'draw_top', so Nostalgia (powers.py:3595-3612) runs FIRST and can move the Skill to the top of the draw pile, after which Corruption's `card in player.discard_pile` test fails (powers.py:610) and the Skill is never exhausted. In C# both are listeners on ONE chain and the last writer wins, so Corruption exhausts it. Both Nostalgia and Corruption are ported Ironclad-pool powers, so the contention is reachable; which one wins in C# is hook_dispatch G2's listener-order question and is not re-verdicted here. (ii) EVENT TIMING: Feel No Pain and Dark Embrace see on_card_exhausted fired from the middle of Corruption's on_card_played rather than at pile assignment, so their effects land after any on_card_played listener registered before Corruption. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
